name: Photon Broom
subtitle: a ground laser that nudges space junk aside

effects.effect: a laser makes sodium atoms high in the sky glow as an artificial star for correcting blur
light pushes on what it hits

effect: a laser makes sodium atoms high in the sky glow as an artificial star for correcting blur
how: A chain reaction of collisions could make low orbit unusable, and most debris is too small and numerous to catch. A powerful ground laser fired through a telescope pushes on a piece of junk with the pressure of light, slowing it a little on each pass so it misses a satellite or falls sooner; a laser guide star lets a flexing mirror cancel the air's blur so the beam stays tight hundreds of kilometres up.
obstacle: Light's push is so feeble that each dodge takes hours of tracking over many nights, and the beam must never dazzle aircraft or other satellites.
why: Proposed by NASA in 2011; ground stations track debris by laser but have never nudged any.
real: NASA Ames LightForce studies and an Australian SERC programme proposed ground-laser photon-pressure debris nudging, with tracking tests but no demonstrated nudge.
